beats.say: Twelve dots are shared into three equal rows. How many dots belong in each row?
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: 12 dots in 3 equal rows. How many dots are in each row?

beats.say: A row runs across. Put four dots in the first row.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Equal rows have the same number of dots. Four here, and four here.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Dots lined up in equal rows form an array. The total is all the dots together.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.meaning: Objects lined up in equal rows.

beats.say: Four plus four plus four is twelve. Multiplication counts the equal rows: three times four is twelve.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Three counts the rows. Four counts the dots in each row.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Division finds the missing row size from the total and the number of equal rows. The sign means divided by.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Twelve divided by three is four. Three rows of four use all twelve dots.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: This array has thirty dots in six equal rows. How many dots are in each row?
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: This array has 30 dots in 6 equal rows. How many dots are in each row?

beats.say: I count six visible dots. My guess is six in each row.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Those dots run down, one per row. Six counts the rows.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: We need the number across each row. The box stands for that missing number.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: The box stands for a missing number.

beats.say: Thirty divided by six asks: six rows of how many make thirty?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: I cannot see across. Can we count by six?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: A column runs down. Each new column gives every row one more dot, adding six dots altogether.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: One more in every row adds 6 dots.

beats.say: One in each row uses six dots.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Two in each row uses twelve dots.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Three in each row uses eighteen dots.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Four in each row uses twenty-four dots.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Five in each row uses thirty dots. All the dots are used.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Five is the number across each row. Six was the number of rows.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: A factor is a number we multiply. Six times five makes thirty, so five is the missing factor.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The answer to a division is called the quotient. Here, it is five dots in each row.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Check by multiplying: six rows of five dots make thirty dots in all.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: A teacher sets out eighteen chairs in three equal rows. How many chairs are in each row?
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: A teacher sets out 18 chairs in 3 equal rows. How many chairs are in each row?

beats.say: One dot stands for one chair. Three rows are given; the number in each row is missing.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: So I need three times some number to make eighteen.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Three times six is eighteen. See six chairs across every row.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: There are six chairs in each row.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Check the story: three equal rows of six chairs use all eighteen chairs.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: What is eighteen divided by nine?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: There is no story. Which number is the total?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: The total goes first: eighteen. We can share it into nine equal rows and find how many in each.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Nine times what number makes eighteen? One column uses nine dots. A second uses all eighteen.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Two dots in every row. Eighteen divided by nine is two.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Nine rows of two make eighteen, so the multiplication checks the division.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Six times nine equals fifty-four. Use this fact to find fifty-four divided by nine.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: We were dividing by the row count. Is nine the number of rows here?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Here, make rows with nine dots in each. We want how many rows use all fifty-four dots.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The given fact tells us: six rows of nine make fifty-four. These are those six rows.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Six counts the rows. Nine counts the dots in each row. This time the missing number counts rows.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: A letter can stand for a missing number too. Here, x stands for the number of rows.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: $x$ stands for the number of rows.

beats.say: Solving an equation means finding a number that makes both sides equal. Six makes both sides fifty-four.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Both sides name the same amount.

beats.say: Fifty-four divided by nine is six. Six rows hold all the dots when each row holds nine.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Check: six rows of nine dots make fifty-four dots in all.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Nine dots go into three equal rows. How many dots are in each row?
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: 9 dots in 3 equal rows. How many dots are in each row?

beats.say: Could the missing factor also be three?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Test it. Three in the first row, three in the second, and three in the third use nine dots.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Three times three is nine. Nine divided by three is three.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: The two factors can have the same value. Three rows of three use all nine dots.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: What is fifty-six divided by eight? Champ, use the array to explain your answer.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Fifty-six is the total. Eight is the number of rows. I need the number in each row.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: I know eight times five is forty. That gives five dots to each row.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: One more in every row adds eight dots: forty-eight.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Another eight makes fifty-six. That is seven in each row, with no dots left over.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: How can you check the whole array at once?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Eight times seven is fifty-six, so fifty-six divided by eight is seven.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Explain how division and multiplication fit together.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: I start with the total and one side of the array.
beats.speaker: learner

do.text: Find the total and the side you know.

beats.say: Division asks for the missing side. I find the factor that makes the total.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: I multiply the two sides to check that they make the whole total.
beats.speaker: learner

do.text: Multiply back to check the total.
